facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's strategy of July 2021 says the national health information system (SNIS) is semi-electronic, computerised at the level of the regions on GESIS, with data passing from districts to regions by hand or by e-mail; the keying level it names is the region, above the district.

The strategy states that the Ministry of Health is deploying DHIS2 under the supervision of its Direction de l'Information et des Statistiques Sanitaires (DISS), which is to be responsible for operating the SNIS databases.

The Stratégie Nationale de Santé Numérique 2022-2026 names DHIS2 in project P221, strengthening and extension of the SNIS with DHIS2, scheduled January 2022 to December 2025 and costed at USD 0.60 million, and recommends DHIS2 as the single SNIS for the whole ministry including the vertical programmes.

The strategy says the DHIS2 deployment is financed by the Global Fund, and its financing table puts the whole USD 0.60 million of the SNIS extension project against technical and financial partners, with nothing against the Ministry of Health.

As at July 2021 the Ministry of Health was in the course of deploying DHIS2 with Global Fund technical and financial support, the one part of the previous digital health strategy's action plan carried out, the rest having gone unimplemented for lack of funds.

The Ministry of Health's strategy of July 2021 states that the electronic patient record (Dossier Electronique du Patient) does not exist in the country, listing it with telemedicine, m-health applications and online training as components that are absent.
